question:
An engineer is implementing an import operation in Cisco UCS Manager.
What is the impact of performing this operation?
options: Information is modified on the management plane only.
A configuration is imported from a higher release to a lower release.
It is possible to schedule an import operation.
Only a configuration file that was exported from the same Cisco UCS Manager is allowed to be imported.
explanation:
Import Configuration - You can import any configuration file that was exported from Cisco UCS Manager. The file does not need to have been exported from the same Cisco UCS Manager.
The import function is available for all configuration, system configuration, and logical configuration files. You can perform an import while the system is up and running. An import operation modifies information on the management plane only. Some modifications caused by an import operation, such as a change to a vNIC assigned to a server, can cause a server reboot or other operations that disrupt traffic.
theory: An import in Cisco UCS Manager applies a previously exported XML configuration file back into the system while it is up and running; because the file only contains system/logical configuration objects (not runtime state), the import only modifies information held on the management plane. Cisco UCS Manager accepts any configuration file that was exported from any Cisco UCS Manager instance (it does not have to be the same one), imports cannot be scheduled, and a higher-to-lower release import is not guaranteed — these are the distinguishing traits tested here. Some imported changes (like a vNIC reassignment) can still trigger a server reboot as a side effect. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 14 — UCS Configuration Management, Import Configuration)
